feed.title: Blog | Abdelwahab Mahmoud
feed.subtitle: Case studies and notes from building production systems.

entry.title: Pulling fulfillment out of the monolith
entry.summary: Fulfillment came out of a PHP monolith one piece at a time, over SQS behind a REST contract, because a team of six could not freeze features.

entry.title: From empty repo to beta launch
entry.summary: A marketplace from nothing to beta: React and Rails, calendar integrations, and CI pipelines from the first week, not as a cleanup later.

entry.title: One backend, drivers on the road
entry.summary: React Native apps fed by one Node.js backend. Live orders reach drivers on phones and the same state reaches the web, over Socket.IO.

entry.title: 7.33M rows per call
entry.summary: One status broadcast ran 1,013 queries and pinned Aurora at 100% CPU. The fix was not an index. EXPLAIN showed each call scanning 7.33M rows.

entry.title: One engine, three providers
entry.summary: Rate limits caused 65% of review failures. Treating them as "retry later" stopped provider outages from becoming ours.

entry.title: Draining, not stopping
entry.summary: ECS scale-in was killing 2-hour translation jobs. So workers drain before they stop.

entry.title: The verdict lives in code, not the prompt
entry.summary: Almost trusted a plausible explanation. So pass/fail had to live in tested code.
